history.summary: POSSIBLE DUPLICATE of seq 1162 ("Kalyaneshwari Temple", Kalyaneshwari, Paschim Bardhaman, West Bengal) — same real temple. TOWN AND STATE CORRECTED: the CSV row says Dhanbad, Jharkhand, but this temple stands at Kalyaneshwari village near Asansol in PASCHIM BARDHAMAN district, WEST BENGAL, on the West Bengal-Jharkhand border by the Barakar River, about 5 km downstream of the Maithon Dam. It is a circa-500-year-old centre of Shakti worship; legend says human sacrifices were offered here in the remote past. The present temple is not very old — Wikipedia says it was built by Sri Gurudin Prasad Pal, while other sources credit the Panchkot Raj (a traveller review claims King Harigupta built the first structure — CONFLICT). The goddess is believed to be a living deity who fulfils the wishes of childless women. The name 'Maithon' is locally derived from 'Mai ka Sthan' (the Mother's place).

name: Kalyaneshwari Temple
town_description: Kalyaneshwari is a small town near Asansol in Paschim Bardhaman district, West Bengal, sitting right at the West Bengal-Jharkhand border on the Barakar River. It lies about 5 km from the Maithon Dam and reservoir of the Damodar Valley Corporation, just off the NH-19 (Grand Trunk Road) bypass. The town is best known for the centuries-old Maa Kalyaneshwari Shakti shrine, which draws pilgrims from both West Bengal and Jharkhand, and the name 'Maithon' itself is locally derived from 'Mai ka Sthan' (the Mother's place).
